name: Norwegian Refugee Council: advocacy and information (charityevals' estimate)
summary: The Norwegian Refugee Council's advocacy and information work (NOK 256 million, $25 million, in 2025): campaigning for humanitarian access and against the 2025 funding gap, media work and the Internal Displacement Monitoring Centre's data. It publishes no measured result, so both branches are built from ranged judgments and counted at half by the shared missing-data slider: access gains in Sudan and the DRC as the extra humanitarian aid they let reach people in the areas covered (about nine tenths of the result), and NRC's share of the aid NGOs' funding advocacy kept or added, net of the aid it displaces, plus a judged share for its other work. It comes to about 0.39 years of healthy life per $1,000 (combined range 0.02-8.5), about the same as charityevals' Save the Children advocacy model; the result is mostly uncertainty, judgments on how much aid access gains unlock and NRC's part in them driving it.

sections.title: Cost
sections.explainer: What the modelled program cost in the year the outcomes below are counted for, including its share of overhead. From audited financial statements or the annual report.

sections.title: Reach
sections.explainer: How many people, animals or meals the spending reached in the same year, as the charity reports it.

sections.title: Effect per unit
sections.explainer: What the intervention does for each unit reached, from the best available studies, before any adjustment.

sections.title: Adjustments
sections.explainer: Discounts for weaker evidence, what would have happened anyway, credit shared with others, and delivery falling short. All multiply the outcome.

sections.title: Value of a dollar moved (shared)
sections.explainer: charityevals' shared method for money a meta charity moves, the same rows in every such model (docs/normalization.md 2.8). A dollar moved is worth what the charities it reaches achieve, each at its live result on this site under your values; new money counts in full, shifted money only for the gain over where it would have gone.

sections.title: Career changes
sections.explainer: People the charity moves into high-impact jobs: per career changed, the pay they give up for the years they stay, valued at the new employer's live result per dollar, times the share of changes the charity caused (docs/normalization.md 2.8). The mirror of staff pay below market.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.explainer: The outcome in the family's shared unit, per dollar.

sections.title: Your dollar's share
sections.explainer: Staff who earn less than they could elsewhere pay part of the cost in kind. With credit by share of resources, your dollar is credited with its share of the full cost only.

rows.explainer: Kroner at the IRS's 2025 yearly average (@fx.usd_per_nok_2025). The programmes are charityevals' NRC programmes model (norwegian-refugee-council-charityevals).

rows.explainer: All of NRC's costs, as in its programmes model.

rows.label: Direct costs on humanitarian activities, 2025 (US$)
rows.explainer: Programme lines, NORCAP and advocacy and information (note 5).

rows.label: Overhead multiplier (total ÷ direct programme costs)
rows.explainer: Spreads project support, administration and fundraising over the lines in proportion to their cost: about 1.10.

rows.label: Cost of advocacy and information, including overhead
Average yearly advocacy spending over the campaigns' years, relative to 2025
rows.explainer: The access gains below come from campaigns over more than one year, set against the average real spending of those years over 2025's (estimate_basis past_average, Convention 11). Anchor: NOK 253.1m in 2024 and 255.8m in 2025 (Activity Accounts); earlier years weren't read, so 1 (0.9-1.15).

rows.label: Access: people in need in Sudan and the DRC, 2025

source.title: Norwegian Refugee Council, Annual Report from the Board 2025 (published 18 June 2026)

rows.explainer: Sudan 30 million (p. 23) and the DRC 21 million (p. 18) people in need of humanitarian aid, the two priority crises where NRC reports access gains from its advocacy in 2025 (p. 39). Gaza's are counted through adv_other_wins_ratio.

rows.label: Access: share of the people in need in the areas where the gains apply
rows.explainer: Judgment 15% (5-40%): the gains are partial and local: progress on bureaucratic barriers and a draft access protocol in eastern DRC, the EU's position that access in Sudan isn't contingent on a ceasefire (p. 39), which bears on El Fasher, Tawila and the Darfurs rather than the whole country.

rows.label: Access: people in need in the areas the gains cover
Humanitarian appeals funding received, 2025 (US$)

source.title: ALNAP, The State of the Humanitarian System 2026, 1.1 The reality of funding gaps
source.quote: Only 35% of the total 2025 appeals target was met.

rows.explainer: Funding received against the 2025 UN-coordinated appeals, US$16.6 billion, against a shortfall of US$30.5 billion (ALNAP 2026, from OCHA's Financial Tracking Service).

rows.label: People in need of humanitarian aid worldwide, 2025

source.title: Norwegian Refugee Council, Annual Report from the Board 2025 (published 18 June 2026)
source.quote: prioritising 114 million people out of the 305.1 million people in need

rows.explainer: OCHA's global figure as NRC's board report gives it.

rows.label: Humanitarian funding per person in need per year (US$)
rows.explainer: About $54 a person a year: the appeals' funding spread over everyone in need.

rows.label: Access: extra aid reaching each person, as a share of a year's aid per person
rows.explainer: Judgment 10% (2-30%): fewer bureaucratic impediments, permits and crossings let more of the aid already funded reach people in the areas covered; NRC's own operations in the DRC and Sudan scaled up after the gains (pp. 18, 23). No study measures how much aid access negotiations unlock.

rows.label: Value of a dollar of humanitarian aid, as a multiple of cash to the poor
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.7× (0.3-1.5×) of @cash.uov_per_dollar: aid in acute crises includes life-saving health and nutrition work worth more than cash, and food, shelter and coordination worth less (charityevals' relief models come to about 0.6-3 times cash's value per dollar). Anchors: World Vision's model takes 1× for US aid, Save the Children's advocacy 1× for aid budgets and 0.3× for research-improved spending.

rows.label: Access: value per person in the areas covered per year (units of value)
Access: chance the gains happened
rows.explainer: The gains are reported as made in 2025 (p. 39), so 1; how much was NRC's doing is the counterfactual and attribution below.

rows.label: Access: years the gain counts
rows.explainer: A won change counts the site's shared years brought forward ($win_years_counted, docs/normalization.md 2.9); access gains in conflicts are fragile, which the counterfactual below takes.

rows.label: Access: years until the gain takes effect
rows.explainer: Judgment a quarter of a year (0-1): access gains act as soon as permits and crossings open; a protocol takes longer to apply.

rows.label: Access: discount for the wait
Access: discounted years counted
Access: value of the gains (units of value, before adjustments)
Access: years of advocacy behind the gains
rows.explainer: Judgment 2 years (1-4): Sudan's and the DRC's access advocacy ran through 2024 and 2025 as priority crises.

rows.label: Access: share of advocacy and information spending on these two crises' access work
rows.explainer: Judgment 12% (5-25%): access is one of two global advocacy goals and Sudan and the DRC two of three priority crises (pp. 39-40), beside Gaza, the funding gap, protection of civilians, neglected crises, media work and the Internal Displacement Monitoring Centre.

rows.label: Access: value per year of 2025 advocacy spending (before adjustments)
rows.explainer: The gains over the years of campaigning, scaled to all of the line's spending by the access work's share, so the other work is valued at the same rate (adv_other_wins_ratio adds what it wins beyond that).

rows.label: Funding: share of a year's humanitarian funding kept or added by NGOs' collective funding advocacy
rows.explainer: Judgment 1% (0.2-4%): in 2025 donors cut aid sharply regardless (the US, the UK, Germany, the Netherlands); NGOs' advocacy kept some budgets from falling further and steered some to underfunded crises (NRC names gains with Norway's ministry, ECHO and the UK's FCDO, p. 40). Studies of advocacy find budgets rarely move much.

rows.label: Funding: NRC's share of the NGOs' funding advocacy
rows.explainer: Judgment 5% (2-12%): NRC is one of the most visible humanitarian voices (Jan Egeland, 170+ inter-agency leaders), among hundreds of NGOs and networks (ICVA, InterAction, VOICE) and the UN's own appeals.

rows.label: Funding: share of the money kept or added that comes from other aid
rows.explainer: Judgment 60% (30-90%): humanitarian budgets kept are partly taken from development aid within the same aid totals; the rest from donors' general spending. As Save the Children's advocacy model.

rows.label: Funding: value of the year's aid kept or added (units of value, before adjustments)
rows.explainer: Aid kept or added × its value net of the aid it displaces (taken as worth the same per dollar), for one year: a year's advocacy against a year's funding.

rows.label: Other advocacy and information, as a share of the two branches' value
rows.explainer: Judgment 30% (0-100%): Gaza access and aid restrictions, protection of civilians and system reform (the Humanitarian Reset), the Neglected Displacement Crises report, and the Internal Displacement Monitoring Centre's data that responders plan with (p. 10); NRC's media work also raises its own funds, which is in its programmes model.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment, access
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.8 (0.5-1): the gains are NRC's own report of partial progress; aid per person and its value are averages.

rows.label: Access: share of the gains that wouldn't have come without the advocacy
rows.explainer: Judgment 20% (5-50%): access in Sudan and the DRC moves mostly with the fighting and the parties' interests; advocacy brings some gains forward or makes them stick, and some lapse within the year.

rows.label: Access: NRC's share of the advocacy behind the gains
rows.explainer: Judgment 15% (5-35%): NRC worked with OCHA, UN agencies, other NGOs and donor governments on these negotiations (p. 40); it is one of the larger operational NGOs in both.

rows.label: Missing-data discount, access
rows.explainer: Thin: the people covered, the aid unlocked and NRC's part are judgments, with no measured result. So it is counted less by the shared slider, the same way in every model (docs/normalization.md 2.12).

rows.label: All adjustments, access
Evidence adjustment, funding
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.8 (0.5-1): the funding total is measured; what advocacy moved is a judgment, already in the share above.

rows.label: Funding: share not counted already in the share moved
rows.explainer: 1: the share of funding moved above is already the difference the advocacy made (what would have happened anyway is netted out there, Convention 5), so nothing more here.

rows.label: Missing-data discount, funding
rows.explainer: Thin: the money moved and NRC's share are judgments. Counted less by the shared slider (docs/normalization.md 2.12).

rows.label: All adjustments, funding
Evidence adjustment: outcome-weighted average of the branches
rows.formula: (acc_value_per_year * acc_total_adj * acc_evidence_adj + fund_value_per_year * fund_total_adj * fund_evidence_adj) / (acc_value_per_year * acc_total_adj + fund_value_per_year * fund_total_adj)
rows.explainer: Each branch applies its own row; this is their outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only.

rows.label: Counterfactual: outcome-weighted average of the branches
rows.formula: (acc_value_per_year * acc_total_adj * acc_counterfactual_adj + fund_value_per_year * fund_total_adj * fund_counterfactual_adj) / (acc_value_per_year * acc_total_adj + fund_value_per_year * fund_total_adj)
rows.explainer: Each branch applies its own row; this is their outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only.

rows.label: NRC's share of the resources: outcome-weighted average of the branches
rows.formula: (acc_value_per_year * acc_total_adj * acc_attribution_share + fund_value_per_year * fund_total_adj * fund_attribution_share) / (acc_value_per_year * acc_total_adj + fund_value_per_year * fund_total_adj)
rows.explainer: Each branch applies its own row; this is their outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only.

rows.label: Share of credit used
rows.explainer: The outcome-weighted average of the branches' shares (acc_attribution_share, fund_attribution_share), for reading only: each branch applies its own.

rows.label: Missing-data discount: outcome-weighted average of the branches
rows.formula: (acc_value_per_year * acc_total_adj * acc_missing_data_adj + fund_value_per_year * fund_total_adj * fund_missing_data_adj) / (acc_value_per_year * acc_total_adj + fund_value_per_year * fund_total_adj)
rows.explainer: Each branch applies its own row; this is their outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only.

rows.label: All adjustments: outcome-weighted average of the branches
rows.formula: (acc_value_per_year * acc_total_adj * acc_total_adj + fund_value_per_year * fund_total_adj * fund_total_adj) / (acc_value_per_year * acc_total_adj + fund_value_per_year * fund_total_adj)
rows.explainer: Each branch applies its own row; this is their outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only.
